speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Members have asked various questions on these cases, which I will address in this Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: SMC has taken steps to appeal the DT's decision.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Court will review this case and evaluate the decision of the DT, including the appropriateness of the fine.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: SMC has taken steps to pursue an appeal against the DT's decision in this case as well.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On appeal, the Court will review the surrounding facts, including the circumstances in which the memorandum was procured and obtained by a family member.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As both these cases are still before the Courts, I shall refrain from referring to them in detail.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It will, however, be clear to Members that the Ministry of Health (MOH) is also deeply concerned with the decisions in both cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH has asked SMC to consider an appeal and SMC has done so.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must, and will, deal with the issues that have arisen to restore and ensure confidence.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Court of Appeal’s decision in the civil suit concerned a case of negligence against CGH for delaying the diagnosis of a patient’s cancer.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I am saddened to learn that the patient Ms Noor Azlin Abdul Rahman has just passed away this morning.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The hospital will extend our support to the family.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Court of Appeal's decision has been interpreted by the medical profession to mean that, in the majority of cases, radiologists are well placed to decide which specialist or hospital department should follow up on a radiological report with an adverse finding.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is different from the current general practice, which is to return the radiological and test reports to the doctor and team who had seen the patient, ordered the investigations and had the continuing obligation to care for the patient.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Radiologists are understandably worried that they do not have the same care relationship with patients and are not in a position to decide which department or specialist is most appropriate for the continuing care of the patient.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our lawyers have told us that the medical profession may not have interpreted the Court of Appeal's decision correctly.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Nevertheless, we must deal with the medical profession’s concerns and clarify the position.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: My Ministry will address them decisively, while always putting patient safety and welfare first.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have to act decisively because these concerns, if unresolved, will, over time, engender the practice of defensive medicine.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will not only affect doctors, but ultimately compromise the quality of medical care, raising medical costs and harming patient welfare.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I will set out a broad overview of these issues and then outline the initiatives to address them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The SMC is a Statutory Board and a self-regulating body, made up of both elected and appointed medical professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Its primary objective is to protect the welfare and safety of patients by regulating the professional and ethical practice of registered medical practitioners and by upholding high standards in the medical profession.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: When a patient makes a complaint, a Complaints Committee (CC), drawn from a panel of 100 senior doctors and 50 laypersons, reviews the complaint and decides on the appropriate further actions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: When needed, the SMC will appoint a DT to hear the case.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Both CCs and DTs are made up predominantly of doctors, aided by specialists who provide expert opinions, as well as legal professionals and laypersons, as appropriate.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The SMC Council members do not sit on the DT, so that the DT can act independently of the SMC.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Most are resolved at the CC stage with about 8% being referred to DTs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As professionals, doctors have to make care decisions in the best interests of their patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: More often than not, they have to rely on their professional judgement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Therefore, what is appropriate in each case is determined by their peers, taking into account what is acceptable practice.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is important to maintain the confidence of both the doctors and the public in this system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Both must have full confidence in the transparency and fairness of the process and outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, the recent cases which I described earlier have cast doubts on this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have to address these concerns directly, make the necessary changes and give appropriate guidance so that there are greater clarity and consistency.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I will now outline some of the main problems which have arisen in the operation of the current system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Delays are unfair to the complainant who would be looking for closure.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is also unfair to the doctor, as it may prejudice the doctor's defence, affect his practice and livelihood, and cause unnecessary anxiety.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If there is an appeal by either party to the Court of Three Judges, further time will be taken up.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Whilst SMC has been making efforts to clear cases faster, the overall process generally takes too long, and some cases experience prolonged delays that are egregious and wholly unacceptable.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second, SMC has faced challenges in engaging doctors to serve on the Complaints and Disciplinary Committees, or as experts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is partly due to the small community of senior practitioners and partly due to the difficulty in securing the commitment of experienced practitioners to serve, because of the heavy time commitment and opportunity cost incurred.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I am most grateful to the doctors who have served on our CCs and DTs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will have to improve and strengthen the system to better support them as they carry out their duties.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Third, despite the guidance in SMC's Ethical Code and Ethical Guidelines (ECEG), there is wide variance in interpreting standards of care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Whilst the Guidelines cannot cater for all scenarios, we need greater clarity on the application of the standards in specific situations, such as the communication of medical information to patients’ family members and the taking of informed consent.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Fourth, there is the issue of consistency and fairness of sentences meted out.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some sentences are not commensurate with the circumstances of the case.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Despite their best efforts, some DTs are too lax, whilst others are too draconian and the SMC has had to appeal to the Court against the sentences meted out in these cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The two recent DT cases, for instance, involve unexpectedly high fines.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But there have also been cases where DTs imposed sentences that were too low, and the SMC has had to appeal to the High Court to increase these sentences.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have to do a thorough review of the existing structure and process, and consider what is the best way in which complaints against doctors should be dealt with, which will minimise the current problems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The workgroup is co-led by Assoc Prof Ng Wai Hoe, Medical Director of National Neuroscience Institute and Deputy Chairman, Medical Board at SingHealth, and Ms Kuah Boon Theng, a Senior Counsel, who specialises in medico-legal cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The workgroup has a broad mandate to review the entire process and make recommendations to my Ministry.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A series of engagement sessions have already been planned.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The first few townhalls were conducted last week with SingHealth on Thursday and Gleneagles on Friday, and another session is planned with NUHS this week.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These consultations will continue as we want to canvass as many views as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition to the workgroup, MOH had also set up a Sentencing Guidelines committee to set out principles and guidance for sentences, to ensure greater consistency and fairness in the sentences meted out by the DTs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This committee has started its work and is expected to also report by the end of the year.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is the process by which doctors provide patients with relevant and material information about the recommended course of treatment, potential risks of the treatment and possible alternatives, to enable the patient to make an informed decision with regard to his care options.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The law on informed consent has, for a long time, been based on the well-known Bolam test, which has been consistently affirmed in Singapore, including by the Court of Appeal in the case of Gunapathy in 2002.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This landmark decision set out the standard clearly.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Over the years, the test was clear and well understood by the medical profession.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In 2017, the Court of Appeal departed from its earlier decision of Gunapathy and applied a modified version of the test formulated in the United Kingdom case in Montgomery versus Lanarkshire Health Board.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The court has ruled that a doctor, in taking proper informed consent, has to provide such information as that particular patient objectively requires.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The feedback from the medical profession is that doctors are not sure as to how to apply the new legal test in practice settings.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There are uncertainty and concern among doctors as to exactly what information would be considered to be relevant and material from the patient's perspective, and when and how consent needs to be taken.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In the current climate of uncertainty, there is a real risk that medical practitioners will adopt defensive medicine.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There is evidence that this is already happening.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Fearing that they might be called out should a complication occur, doctors are likely to overwhelm patients with voluminous information on multiple unlikely risks, protecting themselves legally but confusing patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This would be highly detrimental to Singapore's healthcare system and will damage the trust between doctors and their patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We should guard against turning into the kind of society where doctors care more about not being sued or disciplined by the professional body than about the patients' well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is a well-travelled road elsewhere with very predictable consequences.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The United States is a prime example of a healthcare system where large sums are awarded for medical negligence, a significant fraction of healthcare costs goes towards medical indemnity insurance, and patients and society as a whole end up bearing these costs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will address this and provide clarity and guidance in two ways.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They will evaluate the local practice in different settings as well as study the practices in other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The workgroup will also consult widely on this and seek views from the medical community as well as the public.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It will make recommendations to the Government on every aspect of informed consent and give guidance to the medical profession on what, where and how in taking informed consent.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The intent is to address the needs of the patients while providing the medical community with clear practical guidelines so that doctors do not have to second guess what is needed in each case.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It will also consider whether legislation will be necessary in order to achieve these objectives and to set out the test to be applied.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We should, however, remember that the relationship between the doctor and patient is not only unique in each case, but also dynamic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It will evolve over time and change with each diagnosis and advice given.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is, therefore, not possible nor desirable to be overly prescriptive in such guidance.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There must always be sufficient flexibility in any test or guidance which we formulate so that, ultimately, patient interests are best served.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Doctors know that patient welfare must be paramount.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We aim to give healthcare professionals more certainty on aligning their practices with the rest of the healthcare community and on discharging their ethical and legal obligations to their patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, on the issue of informed consent, the guidance would explain what nature of information would be considered to be relevant and material to patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Such guidance will not be confined to the issue of informed consent.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The approach will be balanced, protecting patients' interests and welfare, yet being fair to doctors.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There should also be consideration for practical issues, such as what to do in emergency situations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH will engage the medical community and public before issuing the guidance.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Court of Appeal’s central concern in that case was to ensure that radiological reports with adverse findings are followed up with appropriate speed and care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This ensures patients’ safety, and we agree entirely with that.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The question, however, is how best to achieve this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Arising from that decision, healthcare professionals and institutions have told us that they need clarity on the level of responsibility that radiologists bear.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They also need clarity as to whether radiological reports with adverse findings should be returned to the doctors or teams who had ordered them, or should they be routed to another specialist department for follow-up.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: That has worked well for us, and my Ministry believes that this is probably the best approach.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: That should give greater clarity to the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Doctors are expected to uphold the highest possible standards of professional and safe medical practice where patients' interests are always at the core.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Patients must trust their doctors and be able to rely on them to look after their interests and well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our doctors, in turn, need to be able to practise in an environment where they have clear guidance and are not burdened with the uncertainties and vagaries of unwarranted sanctions or litigation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have quite a lot of work to do to achieve this, but we are confident that we can do so.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will work through the initiatives described earlier to build a better healthcare system for all.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I just want to follow up in the sense that there must be current cases that are still under review by the DT.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: So, will the work of the DT still carry on currently under the current regulations?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Or will it be deferred until the new rules emerge at the end of the year?

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: I have some concern to raise to the Minister.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: I was told that I needed to wait for three to four months to see a commissioner to make a statutory declaration.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: After that, I have to wait for another at least nine months for the CC to look into the case.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: So, in view of the huge backlog which I understand that SMC is trying very hard to clear, is there a current immediate plan to triage some of these complaints so that we do not have errant prescribers that continue to practise and affect the public's safety?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And if the Member has a specific case in mind, do let me know.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We can take it up and see whether we could expedite the case if it is of an urgent nature.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Therefore, going forward, how do you rectify this problem?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For the two specific cases, we have asked SMC to lodge an appeal to the Court of Appeal, and because the cases are still being heard, I will refrain from commenting specifically on the two cases.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I just want to ask, considering the number of cases that SMC has to deal with, are we also looking upstream into the medical education in terms of getting them to know it while they are actually being trained to be doctors, instead of looking at it now at the SMC level?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But I am just wondering whether you are also looking upstream.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Indeed, that is the case and, therefore, even within the current curriculum of our medical training, ethical practices are part of the syllabus our medical students have to go through.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the same time, we are also strengthening our ethical practice and guidelines, as mentioned in my speech, to provide greater guidance to the practitioners.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As Members would appreciate, the medical landscape changes over time, evolves over time, new procedures, new treatment will evolve and doctors and patients have to decide whether they are appropriate or not.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, the guidelines have to change over time as well.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is why it is an ongoing process.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I mentioned in my speech, we are looking into how we can provide greater guidance to both practising doctors as well as patients so that both sides will have a better understanding of what is acceptable practice.
